scope: Leviticus 21–22, all 57 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 21–22. The exact original XML record at 21:5 includes the written and read forms of the verb for making bald patches; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Names the priest as the restricted actor, interprets nefesh as a dead person in context and lets the exception continue across verse labels.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: No priest will make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, Aaron's sons. Tell them: ‘A priest must not make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: No priest shall make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,

verses.rationale: Retains the close-kin exception and all five relatives in the pinned order, continuing the list into verse 3.
verses.before: except for his nearest relatives: his mother, father, son, daughter, brother,
verses.after: except for a close relative: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
verses.tsw_comparator: except for his nearest relatives: his mother, father, son, daughter, brother,

verses.rationale: Preserves virginity, closeness and absence of marriage as separate qualifications, rather than collapsing them into unmarried alone.
verses.before: or his virgin sister who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may make himself unclean.
verses.after: or his virgin sister who is close to him and has not married. He may make himself unclean for her.
verses.tsw_comparator: or his virgin sister who is near to him because she has had no husband; for her he may make himself unclean.

verses.rationale: Retains baal as husband while noting master/leading-man alternatives and the disputed relation to the preceding exceptions; does not silently add wife or in-laws as the object.
verses.before: He will not make himself unclean as a husband among his people and so profane himself.
verses.after: As a husband among his people, he must not make himself unclean and so profane himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall not make himself unclean as a husband among his people and so profane himself.

verses.rationale: Uses the plural priest referent supported by the read form at 21:5 and the surrounding clauses; keeps all three bodily acts and the complete written/read record in the source hash.
verses.before: They will not make a bald place on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their flesh.
verses.after: Priests must not shave bald patches on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or cut gashes in their flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not make a bald place on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated holiness requirement and the food-of-God image, with offerings-by-fire consistent with preceding chapters.
verses.before: They will be holy to their God and will not profane the name of their God, for they bring the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; therefore they will be holy.
verses.after: They must be holy to their God and must not profane his name, because they present the LORD's offerings by fire, the food of their God. They must be holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they bring the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; therefore they shall be holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves the listed statuses and makes the final he explicitly the priest, not the former husband; notes whether prostitute/defiled are separate or linked descriptions.
verses.before: They will not marry a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, nor will they marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
verses.after: They must not marry a woman who is a prostitute or has been defiled, or a woman divorced by her husband. A priest is holy to his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall not marry a woman who is a prostitute or profaned, nor shall they marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.

verses.rationale: Makes the priest the object of the community's regard, retaining both holiness statements and divine sanctifying agency.
verses.before: You will make him holy, for he brings the food of your God. He will be holy to you, for I the LORD who makes you holy am holy.
verses.after: Treat the priest as holy, because he presents the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, because I, the LORD who makes you holy, am holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make him holy, for he brings the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I the LORD who makes you holy am holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps both self- and father-profanation and the explicit fire penalty; adds no age, marital condition or cultic limitation absent from the verse.
verses.before: If the daughter of a priest profanes herself through prostitution, she profanes her father; she will be burned with fire.
verses.after: If a priest's daughter profanes herself through prostitution, she profanes her father. She must be burned with fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the daughter of a priest profanes herself through prostitution, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Unpacks the long relative construction into identification and prohibition, retaining oil on the head, ordination and both mourning acts consistently with 10:6.
verses.before: The priest who is greatest among his brothers, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and whose hand has been filled to wear the garments, will not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
verses.after: The high priest, the one above his fellow priests, has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been ordained to wear the garments. He must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest who is greatest among his brothers, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and whose hand has been filled to wear the garments, shall not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.

verses.rationale: Preserves the high priest's stricter rule, including both parents, without importing the ordinary priest's close-relative exception.
verses.before: He will not go near any dead body; he will not make himself unclean even for his father or mother.
verses.after: He must not go near any dead body or make himself unclean even for his father or mother.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall not go near any dead body; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or mother.

verses.rationale: Retains the sanctuary prohibition and consecrating oil without converting it into a lifetime residence rule; nezer's consecration/crown sense is explained selectively.
verses.before: He will not go out from the sanctuary and will not profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.
verses.after: He must not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, because the consecration of his God's anointing oil is upon him. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall not go out from the sanctuary and shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: States the marriage qualification plainly while preserving the woman's virginity as the explicit condition.
verses.before: He will take a wife in her virginity.
verses.after: The woman he marries must be a virgin.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall take a wife in her virginity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four descriptions and the own-people qualification; does not collapse defiled and prostitute without noting the syntactic alternative.
verses.before: A widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been profaned, or a prostitute—these he will not marry. He will take as wife a virgin from his own people,
verses.after: He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a defiled woman, or a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people.
verses.tsw_comparator: A widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has been profaned, or a prostitute—these he shall not marry. He shall take as wife a virgin from his own people,

verses.rationale: Preserves offspring and the sanctifying singular him, closing both speech levels at the end of these rules.
verses.before: so that he does not profane his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who makes him holy.”
verses.after: He must not profane his offspring among his people, because I am the LORD who makes him holy.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: so that he does not profane his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who makes him holy.”

verses.rationale: Marks the new source speech and preserves Moses as recipient, continuing to verse 17.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the male Aaronic scope, generations, physical blemish and restricted offering action without converting it into total exclusion from the community.
verses.before: “Speak to Aaron, saying: None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a physical defect may draw near to bring the food of his God.
verses.after: “Tell Aaron: ‘Throughout the generations, no man among your descendants who has a physical blemish may approach to present the food of his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to Aaron, saying: None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a physical defect may draw near to bring the food of his God.

verses.rationale: Renders disability descriptively rather than as personal labels; retains four conditions, with the uncertain facial and limb terms documented.
verses.before: For no man who has a defect will draw near: a man who is blind or lame, one with a disfigured face or a limb too long,
verses.after: No man with a physical blemish may approach: a man who is blind, has difficulty walking, has a disfigured face, or has an overlong limb,
verses.tsw_comparator: For no man who has a defect shall draw near: a man who is blind or lame, one with a disfigured face or a limb too long,

verses.rationale: Retains both broken body parts, using the ordinary foot/hand senses and noting that the Hebrew can cover the leg/arm.
verses.before: a man who has a broken foot or broken hand,
verses.after: or a man with a broken foot or hand,
verses.tsw_comparator: a man who has a broken foot or broken hand,

verses.rationale: Preserves six further conditions without confident modern diagnoses; notes the uncertain stature/wasting and skin terminology.
verses.before: a hunchback, a man of unusually small stature, one with a defect in the eye, an itching disease or scabs, or damaged testicles.
verses.after: or a man with a curved back, stunted growth, an eye blemish, itching sores, a skin eruption, or a crushed testicle.
verses.tsw_comparator: a hunchback, a man of unusually small stature, one with a defect in the eye, an itching disease or scabs, or damaged testicles.

verses.rationale: Keeps both repeated restrictions and the intervening blemish clause rather than dropping their emphasis; retains food and fire-offering language.
verses.before: No man among the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a physical defect will draw near to bring the offerings by fire to the LORD. He has a defect; he will not draw near to bring the food of his God.
verses.after: No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a physical blemish may come forward to present the LORD's offerings by fire. He has a blemish; he must not come forward to present the food of his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: No man among the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a physical defect shall draw near to bring the offerings by fire to the LORD. He has a defect; he shall not draw near to bring the food of his God.

verses.rationale: Makes the continuing food entitlement explicit and preserves both levels of holiness without introducing a restriction not stated here.
verses.before: He may eat the food of his God, both from the most holy and from the holy things.
verses.after: He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy offerings and the holy offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: He may eat the food of his God, both from the most holy and from the holy things.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two access restrictions, their stated rationale and plural holy places, leaving the final them available for its source ambiguity.
verses.before: But he will not enter through the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.”
verses.after: But he must not go to the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a blemish. He must not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he shall not enter through the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the message as the object of speaking and retains all three recipient groups.
verses.before: So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
verses.after: Moses told this to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new speech boundary and recipient, with the sentence continuing to verse 2.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the separation verb and moves the relative clause next to offerings; notes that the following instructions specify the conditions for abstention and eating.
verses.before: “Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things of the Israelites that they make holy to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.
verses.after: “Tell Aaron and his sons to keep away from the holy offerings the Israelites consecrate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things of the Israelites that they make holy to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly descent, duration and uncleanness condition; keeps from-my-presence distinct from the more usual from-his-people penalty.
verses.before: Say to them: Throughout your generations, if any one of your offspring approaches the holy things that the Israelites make holy to the LORD while uncleanness is upon him, that person will be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Tell them: ‘Throughout your generations, any man among your descendants who approaches the holy offerings the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while he is unclean will be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them: Throughout your generations, if any one of your offspring approaches the holy things that the Israelites make holy to the LORD while uncleanness is upon him, that person shall be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses the established chapter 13 term without diagnosing leprosy; treats the emitter as a coordinate case, notes the alternative touching-the-emitter reading, and continues the conditions through verse 6.
verses.before: Any man among Aaron’s offspring who has a serious skin disease or a discharge will not eat from the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by a dead person, or a man who has an emission of semen,
verses.after: No descendant of Aaron with defiling skin disease or a discharge may eat the holy offerings until he is clean. If a man touches anything unclean through contact with the dead, or has an emission of semen,
verses.tsw_comparator: Any man among Aaron’s offspring who has a serious skin disease or a discharge shall not eat from the holy things until he is clean. Whoever touches anything made unclean by a dead person, or a man who has an emission of semen,

verses.rationale: Preserves creature versus human contact and generic person's scope; clarifies the last possessive to avoid assigning every impurity to the priest himself.
verses.before: or whoever touches any swarming creature by which he becomes unclean, or any person by whom he becomes unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be—
verses.after: or touches a swarming creature that makes him unclean, or a person who makes him unclean, whatever that person's uncleanness,
verses.tsw_comparator: or whoever touches any swarming creature by which he becomes unclean, or any person by whom he becomes unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be—

verses.rationale: Completes the conditional list with the evening and bathing requirements; the source's resumed toucher is represented by he rather than a repeated full subject.
verses.before: the person who touches any of these will be unclean until evening and will not eat from the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.
verses.after: he is unclean until evening and must not eat the holy offerings unless he bathes his body in water.
verses.tsw_comparator: the person who touches any of these shall be unclean until evening and shall not eat from the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water.

verses.rationale: Keeps sunset as well as washing and makes the subsequent permission and food rationale distinct.
verses.before: When the sun goes down, he will be clean, and afterward he may eat from the holy things, for they are his food.
verses.after: When the sun sets, he will be clean. Then he may eat the holy offerings, because they are his food.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the sun goes down, he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat from the holy things, for they are his food.

verses.rationale: Retains both carcass categories consistently with 17:15 and the priestly prohibition, without changing it into the general population's consequence rule.
verses.before: He will not eat an animal that died by itself or was torn by wild animals, becoming unclean by it. I am the LORD.
verses.after: He must not eat an animal that died on its own or was torn by wild animals, making himself unclean through it. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall not eat an animal that died by itself or was torn by wild animals, becoming unclean by it. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Names the priests as the plural actor and holy food as the likely singular referent; preserves sin, death and divine sanctifying agency, with referent uncertainty noted.
verses.before: They will keep my charge, so that they do not bear sin because of it and die for profaning it. I am the LORD who makes them holy.
verses.after: The priests must keep the charge I have given them, so that they do not bear sin and die for profaning the holy food. I am the LORD who makes them holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall keep my charge, so that they do not bear sin because of it and die for profaning it. I am the LORD who makes them holy.

verses.rationale: Renders zar by priestly-household eligibility, not nationality, and retains both lodger and wage-worker exclusions with a note on the lodger's uncertain status.
verses.before: No outsider may eat a holy thing. A guest of a priest or a hired worker will not eat a holy thing.
verses.after: No one outside the priestly household may eat holy food. Neither a lodger staying with a priest nor a hired worker may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: No outsider may eat a holy thing. A guest of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat a holy thing.

verses.rationale: Makes purchase and slavery explicit while preserving the household-born category and food entitlement; does not euphemize ownership as ordinary employment.
verses.before: But if a priest acquires a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and those born in his household may eat of his food.
verses.after: But a person the priest buys as a slave with his own money may eat it. Those born in his household may also eat his food.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if a priest acquires a person with his money, that person may eat of it, and those born in his household may eat of his food.

verses.rationale: Keeps marriage as the condition and contribution as the specified food category; does not misread outsider as a foreign national.
verses.before: If a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she will not eat from the contribution of the holy things.
verses.after: If a priest's daughter marries a man outside the priestly household, she may not eat the contributions from the holy offerings.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a priest’s daughter marries an outsider, she shall not eat from the contribution of the holy things.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three conditions for return and the repeated outsider rule, without adding a child-support qualification to no offspring.
verses.before: But if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, has no child, and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat from her father’s food. No outsider may eat of it.
verses.after: But if she is widowed or divorced, has no offspring, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat her father's food. No one outside the priestly household may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, has no child, and returns to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat from her father’s food. No outsider may eat of it.

verses.rationale: Makes restitution for food already eaten intelligible and retains the inadvertence condition and precise one-fifth addition, consistent with 5:16.
verses.before: If someone eats a holy thing unintentionally, that person will add one-fifth to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
verses.after: Anyone who eats holy food by mistake must repay it to the priest, adding one-fifth of its value.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone eats a holy thing unintentionally, that person shall add one-fifth to it and give the holy thing to the priest.

verses.rationale: Selects priests as the unspecified plural subject, places Israelites next to their contribution and records the alternative subject in a note.
verses.before: The priests will not profane the holy things that the Israelites contribute to the LORD,
verses.after: The priests must not profane the holy offerings the Israelites contribute to the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests shall not profane the holy things that the Israelites contribute to the LORD,

verses.rationale: Reads causative hishiu as priestly responsibility for others' unauthorized eating; retains guilt/penalty and the final them with its possible people/offerings referents noted.
verses.before: causing them to bear guilt requiring reparation when they eat their holy things, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.”
verses.after: and so cause the people to bear guilt and its penalty when they eat their holy offerings, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: causing them to bear guilt requiring reparation when they eat their holy things, for I am the LORD who makes them holy.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the second speech boundary within the chapter, rather than merging distinct instructions.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains all addressees, both offerer groups and vow/freewill alternatives; lets the requirement continue in verse 19 without attaching the holiness condition to the human offerer.
verses.before: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: Anyone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens in Israel who brings an offering, whether for any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings that they bring to the LORD as a burnt offering,
verses.after: “Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites. Tell them: ‘When anyone from the house of Israel or any foreigner residing in Israel presents a burnt offering to the LORD, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: Anyone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens in Israel who brings an offering, whether for any of their vows or any of their freewill offerings that they bring to the LORD as a burnt offering,

verses.rationale: Keeps male sex, all three domestic species, unblemished status and acceptance on the offerers' behalf.
verses.before: will bring, for acceptance, a male without defect from the cattle, sheep, or goats.
verses.after: it must be a male without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats to be accepted on your behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: shall bring, for acceptance, a male without defect from the cattle, sheep, or goats.

verses.rationale: Retains the categorical blemish restriction and its acceptance rationale without replacing ritual acceptance with aesthetic quality.
verses.before: You will not bring anything with a defect, for it will not be accepted on your behalf.
verses.after: Do not present an animal with a blemish, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bring anything with a defect, for it will not be accepted on your behalf.

verses.rationale: Retains both sacrifice occasions, animal categories and repeated completeness requirement; notes the disputed special-vow/fulfill-vow phrase and does not add a male restriction here.
verses.before: When anyone brings a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering from the herd or flock, it will be whole and without defect to be accepted; no defect will be in it.
verses.after: When someone offers a peace sacrifice to the LORD from the herd or flock, in fulfillment of a vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without blemish to be accepted. It must have no blemish at all.
verses.tsw_comparator: When anyone brings a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering from the herd or flock, it shall be whole and without defect to be accepted; no defect shall be in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves six animal conditions and the repeated altar prohibition, using the same two skin terms as 21:20; leaves the growth's medical identity uncertain.
verses.before: You will not bring to the LORD an animal that is blind, injured, maimed, has a discharge, an itching disease, or scabs. You will not put any of these on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: Do not present to the LORD an animal that is blind, has a broken bone or a mutilated part, or has a growth, itching sores, or a skin eruption. Do not put any of these on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bring to the LORD an animal that is blind, injured, maimed, has a discharge, an itching disease, or scabs. You shall not put any of these on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated exception and vow/freewill distinction without harmonizing it away; renders seh as the flock category that includes sheep and goats.
verses.before: A bull or lamb with an overgrown or stunted limb may be brought as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
verses.after: You may offer an animal from the cattle, sheep, or goats with an overlong or stunted limb as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted in fulfillment of a vow.
verses.tsw_comparator: A bull or lamb with an overgrown or stunted limb may be brought as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.

verses.rationale: Makes the implied male organs explicit and retains four injuries and the separate in-your-land prohibition without reducing it to foreign sourcing.
verses.before: You will not bring to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. You will not do this in your land.
verses.after: Do not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn away, or cut off. You must not do this in your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bring to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. You shall not do this in your land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rule limited to such animals and retains both damaged/blemished statements; does not turn it into a ban on every foreigner's offering.
verses.before: Nor will you bring any of these from the hand of a foreigner as the food of your God, for their damage is in them; they have a defect. They will not be accepted for you.”
verses.after: Do not accept any such animals from a foreigner to present as the food of your God. They are damaged and have a blemish; they will not be accepted on your behalf.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor shall you bring any of these from the hand of a foreigner as the food of your God, for their damage is in them; they have a defect. They will not be accepted for you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the third new speech within the chapter, introducing the final timing rules.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Names each newborn species naturally and preserves the mother, seven days and earliest acceptable eighth day without requiring sacrifice on that day.
verses.before: “When an ox, sheep, or goat is born, it will remain seven days with its mother. From the eighth day onward it will be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.after: “When a calf, lamb, or kid is born, it must stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day onward, it may be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When an ox, sheep, or goat is born, it shall remain seven days with its mother. From the eighth day onward it shall be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the parent/offspring pairing, flock-species scope and same-day restriction; does not silently restrict the parent noun to female despite the preceding maternal context.
verses.before: Whether cow or ewe, you will not slaughter an animal and its young on the same day.
verses.after: Whether from the cattle, sheep, or goats, do not slaughter an animal and its young on the same day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether cow or ewe, you shall not slaughter an animal and its young on the same day.

verses.rationale: Keeps thanksgiving distinct from the broader peace-sacrifice timing and renders acceptance consistently with 19:5.
verses.before: When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you will sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.
verses.after: When you offer a thanksgiving sacrifice to the LORD, offer it in a way that will be accepted on your behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, you shall sacrifice it so that you may be accepted.

verses.rationale: Preserves same-day consumption and the explicit no-overnight rule without importing the two-day allowance from 19:6.
verses.before: It will be eaten on the same day; you will leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Eat it that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be eaten on the same day; you shall leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both keeping and doing, using the same direct imperative pattern as prior chapters.
verses.before: You will keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
verses.after: Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves profanation, the passive sanctification of God's name and divine sanctifying action, allowing the identity clause to continue to verse 33.
verses.before: You will not profane my holy name, and I will be made holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who makes you holy,
verses.after: Do not profane my holy name. I am to be held holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who makes you holy,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not profane my holy name, and I will be made holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who makes you holy,

verses.rationale: Keeps the exodus and its relational purpose attached to the LORD of verse 32, followed by the repeated self-identification.
